title: Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery: Monthly Installment of a Direct-Payment Repayment Plan
content:
**Rule.** The monthly installment of a repayment plan paid by direct payment, on a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery**, is the balance to be spread divided by the months it is spread over, taken at the standard rate of 100 percent, rounded up to the cent, and never less than the smallest plan installment of the debt type. The balance to be spread is the debt's outstanding balance, and the months it is spread over are the months stated on the latest repayment plan request on the debt.

## How the figure is assembled

1. The balance to be spread is divided by the months it is spread over.
2. That quotient is multiplied by the rate, taken as a percentage: 100 percent.
3. The product is rounded up to the cent once — any fraction of a cent raises it to the next cent.
4. If the rounded figure is lower than the smallest plan installment of the debt type (in the schedule of repayment terms), it is raised to it.

## Worked examples (hypothetical inputs)

| Outstanding balance | Months on the latest plan request | Quotient at 100 percent | Rounded up | Installment (smallest plan installment of 25.00 USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,500.00 USD | 12 | 208.3333 USD | 208.34 USD | 208.34 USD |
| 1,000.00 USD | 8 | 125.00 USD | 125.00 USD | 125.00 USD |
| 240.00 USD | 12 | 20.00 USD | 20.00 USD | 25.00 USD, raised to the smallest installment |

The smallest installment of 25.00 USD is a hypothetical input here; the figure that applies is the debt type's in the schedule of repayment terms.

**Which request counts?** The latest repayment plan request on the debt, by date of receipt; an older request's months are not used once a later one is on the debt.
